items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: about 9 minutes of it was Joe Maini and Charlie Kennedy, the two alto players, playing two choruses each... Joe Maini is dead... guys that have been working for me for thirty years now

ctx.x: She was and old time movie columnist who could make you or break you, you know, in the movie business. She’d be sitting there. It didn’t make any sense that people were coming to see the band. And we were the heroes. We played — $15 a night and our bar tabs were $23. You’ve got to be an idiot to do that. We were having so much fun. We didn’t care about the music. And that went on for about five weeks in a row. It was Mondays, maybe two nights a week. Then the club owner says, “Why don’t we do this five nights a…

tell you what I need now.” I’m the band leader, there was something I wanted to hear. You know, right or wrong, I wanted to hear something that I wanted. It started with, “You hear how the lead trumpet player, how you can hear him so well?” “Yeah.” I said, “Now let me hear the fourth trumpet player. All four trumpets. On the same level.” I wanted to hear the sound of a band, not protruding notes. Now great, now you hear? In the old days, by the way, it was hard to record the bass. All you heard was boom-boom-…

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Joe Maini was the guy you never had to [inaudible] to. You learned what I wrote about him, about Joe Maini, what he said when it was his birthday with the Dream Band played “Happy Birthday” to him, you heard about the Dream Band.

ctx.x: Um hum. If I put Terry Gibbs and Jack Sheldon and Chubby Jackson in a room together, I wonder what might occur?

Well first you’d have to call the insane asylum. You call the insane asylum and make a reservation at the insane asylum. Because I don’t know it would be a lot of laughs. Talk about — Chubby and I had — a completely differently than Jack and I did. I’ll tell you about Jack. You know Jack could get a little risqué on stage. But when he worked with me he knew that he could not do that. I’m selling music and I’ll be the straight man, and Jack is funny without having to be dirty. You know he’s funny. He’s got a great…

Yes. So we’ve been at this for about an hour, I’ve really enjoyed this. I want to wrap up with a couple of questions. I wonder if you could have done anything else in your life besides being a musician.
